text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
AL-AHRAM

- President Mubarak had important talks yesterday with French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette. After the talks Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said: "We do not accept playing around with peace. The world will not allow that."
- President Mubarak received Youssef Boutros-Ghali, minister of state at the prime minister's office for economic follow-up.
- Foreign Minister Moussa had a meeting on arrangements for the Middle East and North Africa economic conference.

- It has been decided, based on instructions from Mubarak, not to approve the establishment of any more private universities until it is shown that the experiment with the first four private universities is a success.

- It has been decided to offer seven public transport companies to private investment in partnership with the public sector, starting next month. The aim is to attract new investment, improve public transport services and ease the congestion in Greater Cairo, now that the financial restructuring of these companies has been successfully completed. Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid announced this.
He also said it had been decided to offer for rent to international companies all the workshops producing spare parts for buses.

- Franck Goddio, head of the European institute for marine archaeology mission working in Alexandria's eastern harbour, said the mission had identified the old coast line of the city and some of the landmarks of old Alexandria. These include parts of the palace which Cleopatra built for Mark Antony.
AL-AKHBAR
- Chirac threatened to break off his trip to Israel.

- Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid announced that it has been decided to allocate 520 million pounds ($153 million) to buy 1,500 new buses to improve services between cities and provinces in seven public-sector companies.
- President Mubarak has sent South African President Nelson Mandela a message on the latest developments in Middle East peace talks.
- The chairman of the Capital Market Authority said foreigners bought or sold shares worth 1.4 billion pounds on the Egyptian stock exchange in the last six months.
- Electricity Minister Maher Abaza said electricity prices will be reviewed at regular intervals after the private sector starts to set up power stations. Prices could fall 30 percent.
AL-GOMHURIA
- Moussa, after talks between Mubarak and de Charette, says Israel bears full responsibility for any setbacks to peace.
- The rising sun shone on the statue of Ramses II in the inner shrine at the temple of Abu Simbel for 23 minutes on Tuesday morning. More than 1,000 tourists witnessed the event.
- Defence Minister Mohamed Hussein Tantawi ordered medical treatment for a pregnant Palestinian woman living at the camp in no-man's-land on the Libyan-Egyptian border.
- Rumours of meningitis have reached Alexandria but a Ministry of Education official said they were baseless.
AL-WAFD
- The cabinet meeting today will discuss arrangements for the economic conference.
$1 = 3.40 pounds
